skill.name: error-detective
skill.description: Use TRACE to debug errors, analyze stack traces, investigate failures, and identify root causes across common programming languages.
skill.summary: Structured TRACE workflow for stack trace analysis, log investigation, and root cause debugging.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from fenced documentation examples, JavaScript template literals, sample API calls, and debugging terminology. The only executable helper performs local log parsing and session note persistence, with no hidden network call, prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or command execution behavior found.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger command and network detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Label example blocks clearly as illustrative snippets and keep executable examples separate from narrative guidance.

remediation.issue: The helper script stores debug session notes in local files.
remediation.suggestion: Document the .debug_sessions write behavior near the helper usage section and advise users not to store secrets in notes.

content.value_statement: Errors waste time when teams chase symptoms instead of causes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured TRACE debugging.
actual_capabilities: Applies the TRACE process to collect, analyze, and verify error fixes.
Explains common Python, JavaScript, Java, and Go error patterns.
Helps separate root causes from symptoms in stack traces and logs.
Provides examples for API, database, memory, and CORS failures.
Includes a Python helper for stack trace parsing, log analysis, and session notes.
limitations: It cannot access production systems unless the user provides logs, traces, or code.
It does not replace language-specific debuggers, profilers, or monitoring platforms.
Its helper script writes local session files when session commands are run.
It cannot guarantee a fix without tests in the target project.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production API Failures
use_cases.description: Use the TRACE steps to collect symptoms, inspect responses, and identify the failing service or data path.

use_cases.title: Resolve Async UI Errors
use_cases.description: Analyze promise failures, missing response fields, and timing issues before changing frontend state handling.

use_cases.title: Standardize Incident Debugging
use_cases.description: Give teams a repeatable checklist for triage, root cause analysis, verification, and prevention notes.

prompt_templates.title: Explain This Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single error message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Error Detective skill to explain this error. Identify the error type, likely cause, missing context, and first safe check: [paste error].

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Stack Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the TRACE framework to this stack trace. Find the first application frame, separate symptoms from causes, and list focused checks: [paste trace].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reproduction Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Error Detective to create a reproduction plan for this intermittent issue. Include hypotheses, variables to isolate, logs to gather, and verification steps: [describe issue].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Production Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full TRACE analysis for this production incident. Prioritize impact, probable root causes, tests, rollback options, and prevention actions: [paste incident notes].

output_examples.input: A JavaScript cart update sometimes fails after an API request and reports missing items.
output: Classifies the issue as an async integration failure.
Identifies missing response status handling as the likely cause.
Recommends validating response shape before updating UI state.
Suggests backend timeout checks as a follow-up.

output_examples.input: A Django profile page raises an attribute error when a user has no profile.
output: Finds the root cause in missing related data.
Separates the template symptom from the model relationship issue.
Recommends creating missing profiles and adding a regression test.

output_examples.input: A Go service panics with a nil pointer in an order handler.
output: Reads the panic from the top of the trace.
Points to the first application frame and nil parameter.
Recommends checking caller validation and adding a guard test.

best_practices: Provide the complete stack trace, environment, recent changes, and reproduction steps.
Change one variable at a time and record each hypothesis before testing it.
Verify the fix with the original reproduction path and a regression test.
anti_patterns: Debugging only the last visible error without tracing the original cause.
Patching symptoms before checking input data, state, and environment.
Running helper scripts on sensitive logs without reviewing local output handling.

faq.question: What does TRACE mean?
faq.answer: TRACE means Trace, Read, Analyze, Check, and Execute. It is the skill framework for systematic debugging.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: The examples cover Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Go error patterns.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance. The optional helper script runs only when invoked by the user or agent.

faq.question: Can it help with production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure triage, root cause analysis, verification, and prevention actions from provided incident data.

faq.question: Can it parse logs?
faq.answer: Yes. The included helper script can analyze local log files and summarize errors when run explicitly.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the full error, stack trace, recent changes, environment details, expected behavior, and reproduction steps.
